messages.subject: F3 key does not switch to TMB mode in AD Studio
messages.subject_clean: F3 key does not switch to TMB mode in AD Studio
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to become familiar with Template Model Builder TMB and AD Model Builder ADMB in AD Studio which uses Emacs. I have been working through the user's guide AD Studio: Statistical modelling in ADMB and TMB Version 1.0 (2018-01-22) by Arni Magnusson. I can follow the initial section of the guide focusing on ADMB and the examples run as expected. However, once the guide switches to TMB I encounter a problem. The guide says to press F3 to switch to tmb-mode. However, when I press F3 on my Dell XPS 15 (9570) laptop with Windows 10 the only option offered is to adjust the volume of the laptop's speakers. Apparently if I did manage to switch to tmb-mode I eventually would need to press F2 to switch back to admb-mode. But pressing the F2 key only allows me to adjust the speaker volume as well. Indeed the F2 and F3 keys on my laptop even include a small speaker icon.

Is there an alternative method of accessing tmb-mode in AD Studio? Or perhaps is there a way to switch the laptop's F3 key functionality to activate tmb-mode and the F2 key to activate admb-mode?  I have installed R in c:\gnu\r and have installed the TMB R package. The tmb.el file is located in C:\~\emacs\lisp\tmb.

Earlier I asked this question on the (emacs) Exchange here:

https://emacs.stackexchange.com/questions/59096/f3-key-does-not-switch-to-tmb-mode-in-ad-studio

Then I discovered the following work around:

I had previously noticed that if I double-clicked on an example ADMB file, eg. simple.tpl, then AD Studio would open in ADMB mode. So, I located an example TMB file, simple.cpp, found here: C:\~\R\win-library\4.0\TMB\examples. I moved simple.cpp and simple.R to a new folder C:\demo. When I double-clicked on simple.cpp then AD Studio opened in TMB mode. If I double-clicked on simple.R then AD Studio opened in lmenu-R mode.

So, it appears I can go from one mode to another by clicking on an external file associated with the mode of interest. This is probably good enough. Although being able to switch modes from within AD Studio would seem to be more convenient.

I was able to obtain parameter estimates from simple.R but a few additional questions arose in the process.  I should probably post those other questions separately.

Thank you for any advice regarding switching modes from within AD Studio.

Mark

messages.subject: Re: Using the WITH_LIBTMB in an R package
messages.subject_clean: Using the WITH_LIBTMB in an R package
messages.body_plain:
1. Yes! The way you set up 'tmb_includes.h' and 'tmb.cpp' is the intentional way (setting WITH_LIBTMB to get declarations and TMB_PRECOMPILE to get definitions). It bothers me a bit that you have to redefine a bunch of macros to avoid conflicts with Rcpp. Somtime in the future this should be fixed in TMB but it will have to wait for now.

I have one comment though. Your setup is tied to CppAD and won't be able to take advantage of the future AD library (branch TMBad) which at some point may become the default. This is not a problem: There will be a flag to explicitly select CppAD.

2. I'm not aware of any simple way to reduce the *.so size except by setting the compiler flag as in https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/wiki/FAQ (bottom) which won't be allowed by CRAN. Ideally one would like to eliminate symbol duplicates so that symbols in tmb.o are not present elsewhere, e.g. compare:

nm tmb.o | grep CppAD6ADTapeIdE13RecordCondExp

with

nm *.o | grep CppAD6ADTapeIdE13RecordCondExp

Then compare with with a symbol you actually precompiled.
It would be nice if, sometime in the future, a larger portion of TMB could be precompiled (without performance side effects).

To you suggestion: I think this idea is essentially the same as the (undocumented) macro 'PARALLEL_REGION' defined here

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/07678703541b81966f18f134d7d7cbf5df9e3345/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L346

and used in

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/master/tmb_examples/register_atomic_parallel.cpp

to avoid taping unnecessary operations?

The idea of using lambda functions looks interesting. So far I deliberately avoided relying on C++11 features because until recently C++98 was the default in R.

On Thursday, June 18, 2020 at 5:24:58 PM UTC+2, Benjamin Christoffersen wrote:

> Firstly, thanks a lot for great package. I have saved a tremendous amount of time on my postdoc because of the package.
>
> Description
>
> I have extensively used the TMB package to implement variational approximations for mixed survival models and joint marker and survival models. The package can be found here: github.com/boennecd/survTMB <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB>
>
> Because the project has grown quite a bit, I really needed:
>
> Multiple .cpp files to reduce the compilation time when developing.
> Make my own interface to CppAD with the additional features from TMB (see MGMS.cpp <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/MGSM.cpp>, heritability.cpp <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/heritability.cpp>, and joint.cpp <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/joint.cpp>). Doing this with Rcpp is convenient.
> Have my own CppAD::atomic_base implementations of particular Gauss-Legendre quadrature and Gauss-Hermite quadrature to reduce the memory usage and computation substantially (see snva-utils.h#L71-L503 <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/snva-utils.h#L71-L503>, gva-utils.h#L29-L231 <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/gva-utils.h#L29-L231>, and joint-utils.h <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/joint-utils.h>).
> Have a number other C++ functions which I needed and get access to them with Rcpp.
> Have unit test in C++ with Catch through the testthat package (see the "test-..." files in /src <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/tree/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src> directory).
> The way I have done this it by having a single .cpp which includes TMB.hpp (tmb.cpp <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/tmb.cpp>) while all other files includes a header which defines WITH_LIBTMB (tmb_includes.h <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/tmb_includes.h>) and some macros so I can use TMB with Rcpp.
>
> Questions
> Is this recommend / will this be supported?
> Further, is there a way to reduce the size of the .dll/.so file afterwards? The final packages takes 130 MB on Ubuntu with gcc-8 (though with -g). It might though be because of RcppArmadillo and RcppEigen packages too.
> Another question which might be for a separate post but I will include it here. I implemented the following function here: utils.h#L64-L73 <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/utils.h#L64-L73>
>
> to conditional skip region which anyway are not computed by this thread like e.g. here: snva.cpp#L79-L83 <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/snva.cpp#L79-L83>
>
> This is useful as it reduces the memory requirement both when evaluating the parallel tapes but also the final memory requirement (which I have seen some post about). It also reduced the computation time in my example. I gather something similar is useful in numerous other applications.
>
> The issue is that I heavily rely on the current parallel_region implementation (tmb_core.hpp#L693-L700 <https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/021e4f4eddbaae1d1fe72fd36c37014103d4faac/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L693-L700>). Thus, is this going to be stable or?
>
> Suggestion
> Regarding the later, then maybe one can make a operator() function where the user passes in the lambda functions like below? This might not be too hard to explain and then the instruction would be e.g. in a grouped data settings to tell the user to pass the complete data log-likelihood factor for each group in a separate lambda function?
>
> class parallel_add {
>     double val = 0.;
>     int counter = 0L;
>
> public:
>     template<class F>
>     void operator()(F f) {
>         if(counter++ % 2 == 0)
>             /* no work */
>             return;
>
>         double const new_val = f();
>         std::cout << "Added " << new_val << '\n';
>         val += new_val;
>     }
>
>     operator double() const {
>         return val;
>     }
> };
>
> int main(){
>     parallel_add adder;
>     adder([&](){ return 1.; });
>     adder([&](){ return 2.; });
>     adder([&](){ return 3.; });
>     adder([&](){ return 4.; });
>
>     std::cout << "Final value is " << (double)adder << '\n';
>     return 0;
> }
>
>
> See http://cpp.sh/9vztz.

Running

nm *.so -C -o --defined-only --print-size --size-sort -t d

gives

....
survTMB.so:0000000001188624 0000000000026226 W Eigen::internal::gebp_kernel<CppAD::AD<CppAD::AD<double> >, CppAD::AD<CppAD::AD<double> >, long, Eigen::internal::blas_data_mapper<CppAD::AD<CppAD::AD<double> >, long, 0, 0>, 2, 4, false, false>::operator()(Eigen::internal::blas_data_mapper<CppAD::AD<CppAD::AD<double> >, long, 0, 0> const&, CppAD::AD<CppAD::AD<double> > const*, CppAD::AD<CppAD::AD<double> > const*, long, long, long, CppAD::AD<CppAD::AD<double> >, long, long, long, long)

survTMB.so:0000000002155216 0000000000040102 t ____C_A_T_C_H____T_E_S_T____0()
survTMB.so:0000000012873888 0000000003840000 V CppAD::recorder<double>::PutPar(double const&)::hash_table
survTMB.so:0000000009030400 0000000003840000 V CppAD::recorder<CppAD::AD<double> >::PutPar(CppAD::AD<double> const&)::hash_table

nm *.so -C -o --debug-syms --print-size --size-sort -t d

instead yields

Essentially confirming that it is all debug information.

> > On Thursday, June 18, 2020 at 5:24:58 PM UTC+2, Benjamin Christoffersen wrote:
> > > Firstly, thanks a lot for great package. I have saved a tremendous amount of time on my postdoc because of the package.
> > >
> > > Description
> > >
> > > I have extensively used the TMB package to implement variational approximations for mixed survival models and joint marker and survival models. The package can be found here: github.com/boennecd/survTMB <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB>
> > >
> > > Because the project has grown quite a bit, I really needed:
> > >
> > > Multiple .cpp files to reduce the compilation time when developing.
> > > Make my own interface to CppAD with the additional features from TMB (see MGMS.cpp <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/MGSM.cpp>, heritability.cpp <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/heritability.cpp>, and joint.cpp <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/joint.cpp>). Doing this with Rcpp is convenient.
> > > Have my own CppAD::atomic_base implementations of particular Gauss-Legendre quadrature and Gauss-Hermite quadrature to reduce the memory usage and computation substantially (see snva-utils.h#L71-L503 <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/snva-utils.h#L71-L503>, gva-utils.h#L29-L231 <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/gva-utils.h#L29-L231>, and joint-utils.h <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/joint-utils.h>).
> > > Have a number other C++ functions which I needed and get access to them with Rcpp.
> > > Have unit test in C++ with Catch through the testthat package (see the "test-..." files in /src <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/tree/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src> directory).
> > > The way I have done this it by having a single .cpp which includes TMB.hpp (tmb.cpp <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/tmb.cpp>) while all other files includes a header which defines WITH_LIBTMB (tmb_includes.h <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/tmb_includes.h>) and some macros so I can use TMB with Rcpp.
> > >
> > > Questions
> > > Is this recommend / will this be supported?
> > > Further, is there a way to reduce the size of the .dll/.so file afterwards? The final packages takes 130 MB on Ubuntu with gcc-8 (though with -g). It might though be because of RcppArmadillo and RcppEigen packages too.
> > > Another question which might be for a separate post but I will include it here. I implemented the following function here: utils.h#L64-L73 <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/utils.h#L64-L73>
> > >
> > > to conditional skip region which anyway are not computed by this thread like e.g. here: snva.cpp#L79-L83 <https://github.com/boennecd/survTMB/blob/7f85d03e87963fba40425bdf8c90371fd6a312f0/src/snva.cpp#L79-L83>
> > >
> > > This is useful as it reduces the memory requirement both when evaluating the parallel tapes but also the final memory requirement (which I have seen some post about). It also reduced the computation time in my example. I gather something similar is useful in numerous other applications.
> > >
> > > The issue is that I heavily rely on the current parallel_region implementation (tmb_core.hpp#L693-L700 <https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/blob/021e4f4eddbaae1d1fe72fd36c37014103d4faac/TMB/inst/include/tmb_core.hpp#L693-L700>). Thus, is this going to be stable or?
> > >
> > > Suggestion
> > > Regarding the later, then maybe one can make a operator() function where the user passes in the lambda functions like below? This might not be too hard to explain and then the instruction would be e.g. in a grouped data settings to tell the user to pass the complete data log-likelihood factor for each group in a separate lambda function?
> > >
> > > class parallel_add {
> > >     double val = 0.;
> > >     int counter = 0L;
> > >
> > > public:
> > >     template<class F>
> > >     void operator()(F f) {
> > >         if(counter++ % 2 == 0)
> > >             /* no work */
> > >             return;
> > >
> > >         double const new_val = f();
> > >         std::cout << "Added " << new_val << '\n';
> > >         val += new_val;
> > >     }
> > >
> > >     operator double() const {
> > >         return val;
> > >     }
> > > };
> > >
> > > int main(){
> > >     parallel_add adder;

> > >     adder([&](){ return 2.; });
> > >     adder([&](){ return 3.; });
> > >     adder([&](){ return 4.; });
> > >
> > >     std::cout << "Final value is " << (double)adder << '\n';
> > >     return 0;
> > > }
